- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast decline to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–72), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward correction for days 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
